## Rule

**DECODED 2026-06-01 (v1 rewrite — 100% / 200,000 vs ARC-GEN GT, exactly matches LIVE):**

A bordered rectangle: **A** = frame color (the non-bg color whose cells are 4-connected adjacent to background), **B** = inner fill color (the other non-bg color, strictly interior — never touches bg). The fill rectangle has a small defect, and a "cross-out" is drawn through it; cleared cells become **B** where the cell was background, else **A**. Two defect modes (the generator produces both):

1. **Sparse markers** — one or more rows/cols of B are sparse (B-count < ⅔·max). A B-cell in a sparse *row* clears its *column* (vertical line); a B-cell in a sparse *col* clears its *row* (horizontal line). This covers isolated B-pixels protruding into the frame.
2. **Corner notch** (no sparse markers) — a single 1-cell dent at a corner of the B rectangle. Then cross **all the FULL lines** (B-count == max) along the **shorter bbox dimension** (e.g. a 4×6 bbox with a notch → cross the full rows; a 10×4 bbox → cross the full cols).

The cross paints a full line across the grid: background margins → B, frame/fill cells on the line → A. Padding (outside the active H×W grid) stays all-zero.

**Historical trap (still valid):** `Research_Archive/notes/digest-task383-2026-05-11.md` — the old `task383_v2` was a visible-derived axis-cross-out that matched 266/266 visible but was **hidden-bad** on Kaggle (−12.31 LB). The difference now: the v1 rewrite is validated at **100% against 200k ARC-GEN ground-truth samples** (the hidden distribution), not just the 266 visible pairs, and matches LIVE 266/266. Decode-from-visible-only is the trap; decode-and-verify-against-the-generator is safe.

## Cost analysis

**v6 #98 dilated conv (2026-06-11): cost 10,942 = memory 10,856 + params 86 (points ~15.70). Δ −2,170 vs v5 13,112. Byte-equal to v5/LIVE (ab --full 200266/200266).** (Progression: v1 25,767 → v3 18,666 → v5 13,112 → **v6 10,942**.) The dilated Conv K[1,10,2,2] dilation=6 crops the 30×30 color-decode directly to 24×24 F32 (2,304 B) — replaces cidx_full (3,600 B) + cidx_u30 (900 B). Net memory −2,196; net params +26 (kernel [1,10,2,2]=40 vs old color_w [1,10,1,1]=10 + crop_e[4] removed).

**v8 corrected free-output BitwiseAnd tail (2026-06-21): cost 9,148 = memory 9,010 + params 138, profile 9,148.** This is the cheapest correct Boladi formulation measured in the Where-overlay/free-output family this pass, but it is still **+1,806 above Aditya team-best 7,342**, so it is not staged. It deletes v6's 900-B `canvas30` and the 24x24 output-color planes by generating the full one-hot as `BitwiseAnd(rowbits [1,10,30,1] U8, colbits [1,1,1,30] U8) == output`. The corrected decomposition needs 7 row/col products: two A rectangle-complement terms, three B terms (interior + horizontal/vertical bg stripes), and two channel-0 background-completeness terms. Dominant charged tensors still left: `cidx_f24` 2,304 B, `is_B_h` 1,152 B, `cidx_u` 576 B, `is_B_b` 576 B, plus `rowbits`/row channel-select 1,020 B. The prompt's single-Where overlay is not cheap here because there are **two data-dependent replacement colors** (A inside rectangle, B on background stripes) and channel-0 background must remain complete; a nested full-canvas `Where` would materialize a 10-channel intermediate, while the bitset tail is the cheaper exact free-output form.

**v5 rewrite (2026-06-02): cost 13,112 = memory 13,052 + params 60 (points 15.52).** (Superseded by v6.) v5's per-tensor breakdown is in the floor proof below. The earlier v3 breakdown (kept for reference):
